about: Reviewed, per-landmark corrections layered on top of the open data, never written back into it. geometry: which open-data features ARE the landmark (Overture building ids, OSM ids), used instead of any nearest-footprint search. authoritativeHeight: a published height that replaces an incomplete or estimated height for exactly those features (in the derived pack only). model: an original, approximate structural model drawn at the real location from published dimensions, where open geometry is missing or a plain extrusion can't represent the structure. Every value carries its source. Read by scripts/earth/build-region.mjs (heights), scripts/earth/build-landmarks.mjs (geometry, models) and, through landmarks.json, the renderer (space/earth/landmark-models.js).

geometry.note: Drawn from its 36 OpenStreetMap building parts (setbacks 15–828 m).

authoritativeHeight.measurement: architectural height to the top of the spire
authoritativeHeight.source: Wikidata Q12495 P2048 (829.8 m; CTBUH architectural height). OpenStreetMap's spire part says 828 m.

geometry.note: OpenStreetMap's Elizabeth Tower outline says 96 m, but its tallest building part stops at 91 m: the open data disagrees with itself.

authoritativeHeight.measurement: to the top of the spire finial
authoritativeHeight.source: UK Parliament ('The Elizabeth Tower … is 96 m tall'); Wikidata Q41225 P2048 96 m; OSM outline height=96

Q402937.name: Ahsan Manzil

geometry.note: OSM way 624025793 (historic=building, name=Ahsan Manzil) — Overture 43773ae3 is the same polygon (17 vertices, 1433 m²). OSM relation 8665455 (museum grounds) carries wikidata=Q402937; Wikidata has no OSM id back.

authoritativeHeight.measurement: walls: 1 m platform + 5 m ground floor + 5.8 m first floor

Q402937.partial: The mapped footprint is 54 × 30 m; the published palace is 125.4 × 28.75 m. The width agrees, so the open data appears to hold only the central (domed) block; the wings aren't mapped as part of it and are not invented here.

model.note: Octagonal drum and lotus-bud dome at the centre of the real footprint, to the published 27.13 m; drum size estimated.

Q497536.name: Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban

geometry.note: OpenStreetMap's National Parliament House footprint (via Overture), a single multipolygon for the whole assembly building.

authoritativeHeight.measurement: the eight peripheral blocks (110 ft); the central octagonal block rises to 155 ft = 47.2 m and is not mapped separately

Q497536.sourceDisagreement: Wikidata P2048 gives 155 m: the published figure is 155 ft (47.2 m) for the central block — a unit error in Wikidata, not used.

geometry.note: OSM relation 9596872 is the outline (135 × 181 m bounding box). Its 12 building parts are fragments (a few shells and glass roofs, no heights), so the outline is used as the podium and the shells are modelled.

published.source: Sydney Opera House Trust / Structurae (183 × 120 m; highest roof point 67 m above sea level)

model.note: Original simplified model: podium on the real outline (height estimated, ~10 m per the OSM mapper's note), two halls of four sail-shaped shells each plus the restaurant pair, the tallest reaching the published 67 m above sea level. Shell positions, sizes and orientation are approximate.

published.source: Transport for NSW / Wikipedia (main span 503 m; arch top 134 m above sea level; 49 m clearance; deck 48.8 m wide; pylons 89 m)

model.note: Steel through-arch: two arch ribs, hangers, deck and the four granite pylons, on the axis of the real bridge roads. Truss detail is simplified.

published.source: NYC DOT / Wikipedia (main span 486.3 m; towers 84.3 m above water; 41 m clearance; 26 m wide)

model.note: Two masonry towers, deck and four main cables on the axis of the real bridge roads; arches, stays and suspenders simplified.

geometry.note: The two towers, from their OpenStreetMap building parts (piers, tower bodies to 47 m, tops to 65 m).

published.source: Tower Bridge (City of London Corporation): high-level walkways 42 m above the river

model.note: The two high-level walkways between the real towers (not in the open data), at the published 42 m above the river (≈ 44 m above datum at high water).

geometry.note: OSM node 4919986733 (man_made=monument, wikidata=Q79961) is 0.5 m from Wikidata's coordinate. OSM way 105667349 is the chapel inside the pedestal (Capela de Nossa Senhora Aparecida): its chamfered-square outline, ≈ 8 m across with axes at 80.8°/170.8°, is used as the pedestal footprint. OSM tags it fixme: 'outline needs verification'.

published.source: Wikidata Q79961 (30.1 m statue); Britannica / Santuário Cristo Redentor descriptions (30 m statue, 8 m pedestal, 28 m arms)

orientation.basis: Facing taken along the pedestal's mapped axis (80.8°), toward the city and Guanabara Bay to the east (Botafogo/Urca), back to the Tijuca forest. No official or open source found gives a measured bearing; the axis is from OSM (fixme-tagged) and the eastward facing from general descriptions.

model.note: Original procedural sculpture to the published dimensions (30 m statue + 8 m pedestal = 38 m; 28 m arms) on the real summit location and the mapped pedestal outline. Silhouette is simplified; facing confidence medium-low.
